paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. This father doesn't wait until the young man is standing at her door to give his warning. He starts way back at the beginning: "My son, keep my words and treasure my commandments within you." (Proverbs 7:1). The time to be ready is BEFORE the twilight stroll.

Look at what the father says wisdom is for. He tells his son to say to wisdom, "You are my sister," so that wisdom and understanding "may keep you from the adulteress, from the stranger with seductive words." (Proverbs 7:4-5). Wisdom isn't just a pile of facts you carry around, friend. She's family, the one you call first, and she keeps you from walking in blind.

Then the father closes with a plain plea: "Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways; do not stray into her paths." (Proverbs 7:25). Notice he says the heart turns aside before the feet ever do. So guard your heart now, with God's Word written on it, because a heart that already knows the way home hears the warning in time (Proverbs 7:3).
